key_insight: One expert directing parallel LLM agents ported CompCert’s verified compiler core from Rocq to Lean in about six weeks, completing all 4,908 recorded proof obligations without project-specific axioms.
engineering_relevance: The port demonstrates a path to agent-assisted maintenance and optimization of a formally verified compiler while retaining its end-to-end correctness theorem.
method: Partition the migration along dependency boundaries.
Audit translated definitions and theorem statements before rebuilding proofs.
Reconstruct proofs in parallel against stable interfaces.
evidence_signal: Across 29 small-tests programs and matched 24-active-hour budgets, GPT-6-astra’s Lean candidate reduced generated-program runtime by 11.7% versus original CompCert 3.17, compared with 2.3% for its Rocq candidate.
watch_item: The optimization evidence comes from 29 small test programs, so performance gains may not generalize to larger production workloads.
paper_title: CompCert4Lean: Porting a Verified C Compiler to Lean in Six Weeks with Parallel Coding Agents
